item.title: Reverse-Process Synthetic Data Generation for Math Reasoning
item.dc:creator: admin
item.description: Training LLMs on mathematical reasoning by inverting easy-to-solve problems: generate derivatives, reverse them into integration exercises with full step-by-step solutions.

item.title: SLUUG Talk: Demystifying Large Language Models on Linux
item.dc:creator: admin
item.description: Talk for the St. Louis Unix Users Group about running and understanding Large Language Models on Linux.

item.title: Master's Project: Reliability Estimation in Series Systems
item.dc:creator: admin
item.description: My master's project on maximum likelihood estimation for series systems with right-censored and masked failure data.

item.title: Fine-Tuning a Tiny LLM for ElasticSearch DSL
item.dc:creator: admin
item.description: Fine-tuning a small language model to generate ElasticSearch DSL queries from natural language, as a proof of concept for domain-specific LLM specialization.

item.title: Do Geomagnetic Storms Ground Europe's Night Migrants?
item.dc:creator: Alexander Richard Towell
item.description: A US radar study found 9 to 17% less bird migration on geomagnetic storm nights. Three tests on European weather radar, frozen before the data were downloaded, found no such drop.

item.title: Finding Every Smallest C6-Saturated Graph
item.dc:creator: Alexander Richard Towell
item.description: An eleven-vertex witness, 205 minimum graphs on fourteen vertices, and the difference between finding an example and proving a minimum.

item.title: October Research Notes: Graphs, Proofs, and Experiments
item.dc:creator: Alexander Richard Towell
item.description: Recent work on graph saturation, formal mathematics, and conversational memory, with a few experiments that changed what I thought I was measuring.

item.title: Watch: Calculus, The Big Ideas
item.dc:creator: Alex Towell
item.description: Calculus as one idea examined from every side: a seven-episode animated playlist running from limits through the derivative, the integral, the fundamental theorem, gradients, and optimization.

item.title: The Channel: Animated Series on YouTube
item.dc:creator: Alex Towell
item.description: The metafunctor YouTube channel now carries animated versions of the site's series, built from the same source material with a from-scratch pipeline. Four playlists so far, thirty-seven videos.

item.title: Watch: Algorithms Arise from Algebraic Structure
item.dc:creator: Alex Towell
item.description: The Stepanov series is now a nine-episode animated playlist: declare the algebraic structure, and the algorithms come for free. From the monoid to lattices, in teacher and student dialogue.

item.title: Watch: Inductive Biases, What Your Architecture Assumes
item.dc:creator: Alex Towell
item.description: The inductive-biases series is now a ten-episode animated playlist: every architecture is a bet about the world, and the bet is the bias. No free lunch first, then each architecture read as its assumptions, graded on one scorecard.

item.title: Watch: Next-Token Prediction, from Solomonoff to Transformers
item.dc:creator: Alex Towell
item.description: The sequential-prediction series is now an eight-episode animated playlist: what-comes-next as the foundation of the language-model era, traced from Solomonoff induction to the transformer.

item.title: Watch: Quantum Computing from Scratch, in Python
item.dc:creator: Alex Towell
item.description: The quantum-from-scratch series is now a ten-episode animated playlist: a NumPy simulator built from nothing, amplitude bars you can watch interfere, and a classical on-ramp with the coin under the cup.

item.title: Extremal Graph Witnesses on the House of Graphs
item.dc:creator: admin
item.description: Four extremal graphs deposited to the House of Graphs: a minimum C6-saturated graph and three Zarankiewicz witnesses. Plus two new exact saturation values, verified and prepared for deposit.

item.title: Fifteen Integer Sequences in the OEIS
item.dc:creator: admin
item.description: Fifteen integer sequences now published in the OEIS: nine authored, six extended. Computed by SAT solving and exhaustive search, checked against prior art, spread across seven fields.

item.title: The Unbegotten: A Maker That Believes Itself Uncaused
item.dc:creator: Alex Towell
item.description: A maker that only believes itself uncaused, lonely enough to fill the dark with worlds. On the debt between a creator and the things it creates.

item.title: Measure: Indifference as Arithmetic
item.dc:creator: Alex Towell
item.description: A mind reasons that its own death is the one event it can never undergo, then follows the arithmetic to a monstrous conclusion. On mistaking amplitude for meaning.

item.title: Epilogue: measure and meaning
item.dc:creator: Alex Towell
item.description: The very first useful thing our simulator did, back in post 0, was turn a vector of amplitudes into a vector of probabilities.

item.title: Multitudes: Taking Quantum Mechanics Literally
item.dc:creator: Alex Towell
item.description: Take the quantum equations at face value, refuse the collapse, and you are a branching many the math weighs but never values. On what that leaves of the self.

item.title: On Intelligence: The Gap Where Safety Is Decided
item.dc:creator: Alex Towell
item.description: There is a beautiful, settled theory of intelligence, and there are the crude systems we shipped. The distance between them is where safety is actually decided.
